title: Clarify explicit empty skipped members in completion-seal projections
outcome: Clarify explicit empty skipped members in completion-seal projections
acceptance: docs/features/sqlite-store.md documents, with the exact shapes, that integrity verification (doctor, and the full verification migration import runs before publishing) refuses a completion seal whose work_completion_seals projection or canonical object carries an explicit `obligations: []` or `environment: []` (members the seal type skips when empty), naming the findings each case produces (projection only: completion_seal:<id>:projection_binding and completion_seal:<id>; canonical only: completion_seal:<id>:canonical_representation, reported by both seal checks; both: all of these), while ordinary loads decode such a seal; and a test pins, for each of the two fields, the projection-only, canonical-only and both cases with that exact finding matrix, injecting real JSON [], asserting that normal encoding omits the member, that the omitted-member baseline stays healthy, that an ordinary load decodes the seal, and that verification leaves the stored bytes unchanged

completion.summary: sqlite-store.md now documents that integrity verification requires every stored member to survive being written back. A completion seal stored with an explicit `"obligations": []` or `"environment": []` decodes, but doctor reports it and migration import refuses to publish it. The exact findings: projection only, projection_binding plus the bare seal label; canonical only, canonical_representation from both checks; both, all of these. An ordinary load still decodes such a seal. A new test pins all six cases, the healthy baseline, the ordinary load, and that verification leaves the bytes unchanged. Full gate test-d85f17f5 passed; evaluation 75cd219c 1/1. Landed as a3b8efe and installed as build ef448e9e674e. Follow-ups: w-e736c419c503, w-a426617d5def, w-f1358c5960b6.
